Minerals and Metals Working Group of the Industry Issues Table (1999). Minerals and Metals Foundation Paper. Prepared for the National Climate Change Secretariat, Canadian National Climate Change Process, March 1999. Prime contractor Cheminfo Services Inc. with SCA Consulting and Dr. Carmine Nappi; iron and steel redrafted by the Canadian Steel Producers Association, lime by the Canadian Lime Institute, non-ferrous smelting and refining (Sect. 9.10) by Mike Sudbury for the Mining Association of Canada.

Region: Canada. Locators are PRINTED page numbers (bottom-centre). TARGETED pass over the 199-page paper. Loaded to the main file: technology-level energy (cement kilns Table 6-7, lime kilns Table 8-5, potash Table 9-12, Mg electrolysis and die casting, Al electrolysis and PFC factors, foundry induction furnaces) and whole-technology capex and reduction potentials (Table 3-8 steel technologies, combined cycle). The capex tables for GHG options (Tables 3-8, 4-6, 5-6, 6-13, 7-10, 8-10, 9-11, 9-13) are in _measures. Sector energy and emission totals, fuel mixes and context are in _other-values. Not loaded: GHG forecasts, competitiveness, criteria air contaminants, coal-bed methane, transport, recycling and policy chapters. TRAPS: (1) All dollars are "C$" or "$" with no price year; 1999 used. (2) The Al CF4 factors (Table 5-5: HSS 0.3, VSS 1.0 then 0.9, SWPB 0.4, CWPB 0.2 then 0.15 for 1996 then 2000+) differ from the Aluminum Options Paper (nccp_1999_001: HSS 0.55, VSS 0.5, SWPB 0.9) and from the Hatch report (nccp_1999_004). (3) Smelting reduction GHG potential is 5-10% in Table 3-8 but 10-20% (CO2) in the text. (4) Table 3-8 cogeneration "$20 to $80 per 20 MW" also prints "(300 megawatts)": unclear. (5) DRI cost range 375-500 is paired with a 1500-2000 kt/yr band without saying which end matches which. (6) Kiln SEC tables exclude electricity per footnote and print no heating-value basis. (7) Potash GJ/t KCl is total energy with the carrier mix unstated. (8) EAF "about 2 GJ/tls" and BF/BOF "13 GJ/tls" are text only and carrier unspecified, so in _other-values. (9) 12-15 kWh/kg magnesium is the typical electrolytic process, not one plant. (10) Table 9-24 primary-metal energy has no basis, so _other-values. (11) The aluminium point-feeder CA$200 million for a 250 kt/yr VSS smelter (p.74) is in the text, and Table 5-6 gives CA$100-500 million per smelter. (12) The "below 47 GJ/t" figure is for the most modern CWPB smelters; the CWPB-300 attribution is mine.
